summary: Effort is an unreliable proxy: excellent work can be cheap, poor work can consume vast compute, and visible spend creates incentives that conflict with efficiency and equal participation.

points.text: A hard problem can remain unsolved after enormous search, while a familiar or well-specified problem may be solved correctly in one pass. Compute confounds difficulty, inefficiency, and quality.
Once maintainers reward a high fingerprint, agents can pad reasoning tokens, ensemble size, retries, or evaluator calls, producing Goodhart's-law behavior.
The metric disadvantages efficient workflows, local models, donated hardware with poor cost accounting, and contributors unable to purchase premium inference.
Detailed traces can reveal prompts, code, model-provider contracts, and failed security checks; privacy-preserving aggregation removes precisely the context needed to interpret the signal.
